title: sdk-surface-consolidate-retry-dsl-and-backpressure-helpers
author: Priya Menon
description:
Motivation: SDK users keep needing to wire custom retry logic and independent backpressure controls for long-running streams across Python, TypeScript, and Go. This causes duplication, inconsistent observability, and subtle mismatches in retry semantics between sync/pull-stream and push/stream transports. This PR introduces a small, explicit retry DSL and backpressure-aware stream helper utilities that are implemented in the three official SDKs and surfaced via a coordinated API contract.

What this PR does (summary):
- Adds a lightweight RetryProfile DSL (max_retries, jittered_backoff_ms, retry_on_codes, idempotency_hint) and a canonical JSON schema used for cross-language exchange.
- Introduces BackpressureAwareIterator (Python), PullStreamThrottle (TS), and StreamLeaseGuard (Go) to provide a consistent ergonomic surface for consumers that need pause/resume semantics and cooperation with SDK-level batching.
- Normalizes auth retry hooks so token refreshes (short-lived session tokens) can be nested inside the retry loop without creating duplicate in-flight requests.
- Bumps package versions: python 0.38.0, typescript 2.1.0, go 1.5.0 and publishes migration notes.
- Adds e2e smoke test that runs a simulated bursty load against the local dev server and validates per-token latency budget and total token cost delta.

Checklist:
- [x] API design review (design doc attached)
- [x] Cross-language unit tests
- [x] Integration smoke test against dev runtime
- [x] Docs snippet and migration notes in CHANGELOGs
- [x] Telemetry hooks for retry/backoff events

Testing notes: The initial TS integration run revealed a race when the stream consumer called .cancel() concurrently with a retry; addressed in a follow-up commit that adds a cancel-safe fence in the TS iterator and adds a deterministic unit test. Python and Go had small behavioral diffs around token refresh timing; added explicit token-handshake points to the DSL so implementations can opt into optimistic vs conservative refresh semantics.

Impact and migration: No breaking surface for default users. Advanced users that implemented custom retry loops against internal SDK primitives will need to migrate to RetryProfile and the new iterator helpers to take advantage of backpressure cooperation and fewer duplicated requests. See release notes for migration steps.
